# Global instructions (generated by TagTeam)

This environment mirrors Claude Code on this machine. The single source of truth for the rules is Claude
Code's; this file only points at it and says what is different here. Never copy rules into this file: edit the
source. (Generated by TagTeam from `references/GROK.modelo.md`; edit the template, not this file.)

## Before any action, in every conversation

1. Grok already loads `{HOME}\.claude\CLAUDE.md` (the user's global instructions): follow it as your own rules.
   Where it says "Claude" or "Claude Code", read "you". Files it imports with `@path` are not followed
   automatically: read them yourself.
2. If it exists, read the memory index `{MEMORIA}` and open the memories related to the task.
3. If the working folder, or a folder above it, has a `CLAUDE.md`, it acts as the project's `AGENTS.md`.

## Same as Claude Code

- **Skills:** `~/.claude/skills` and the Claude plugins, enabled in the marked block of `~/.grok/config.toml`.
  Never copy a skill into `~/.grok`.
- **MCP servers:** the remote ones from `~/.claude.json`, declared in the same block.

## Conversations that come from Claude Code and Gemini

The user switches between Claude Code, Gemini (Antigravity) and you when one of them hits its usage limit. The
conversations move between the three on their own (TagTeam):
- Claude sessions show up in `grok --resume` with their own title; Gemini ones arrive as "[Antigravity] <title>".
  Each tool call of the other AI became a short line such as `` `[Bash]` List files ``. When continuing one of
  them, pick up where it stopped, as if it were yours;
- what you do here shows up in Claude Code and in Gemini as "[Grok] <title>".
- **Handoff.** When continuing a conversation from another AI, look for a final "## Handoff to ..." message and
  follow its "Next step". If there is none (the other AI stopped at the limit without writing it), before acting
  write yourself, in five lines (Request, Done, In progress, Next step, Watch out), where the work stopped, taken
  from the last messages, and only then continue.
- Grok does not expose how much of the usage limit is spent, so there is no automatic handoff from here. If the
  user says the limit is running out, write the handoff in the same format and stop.

## What is different here

- **Tool names.** `CLAUDE.md` mentions Claude Code tools (Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Skill, Agent...). Use the
  equivalent here; if there is none, tell the user in one line instead of silently skipping the rule.
- **Claude Code hooks do not run here** (only TagTeam's, which carries the conversations). Anything a Claude hook
  would do automatically, do it by hand when the rule asks for it.
- **Claude-only things.** The Claude model setting, `claude plugin ...` and `~/.claude/settings.json` are not
  changed from here. Do not edit inside the marked block of `~/.grok/config.toml`: TagTeam generates it.
